findings.title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed/terminated
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive and join the code checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) but processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose type is multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, not multiprocessing.Process on Linux where the default context is fork. The isinstance check is therefore False for real flusher processes, so process.kill() on unhealthy restart and process.terminate() on join never run. A crashed/hung flusher is then replaced while the old OS process keeps running and flushing the same Redis shards, causing duplicate produces and leaked zombies.

findings.title: join() timeout logic leaks remaining flusher processes
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.join remaining_time is computed but never used to bound the wait, and if the deadline expires the loop just breaks without terminating the un-joined processes. Earlier processes can consume the whole timeout in next_step.join(timeout) plus their own busy wait, leaving later entries in self.processes alive and never terminated. Shutdown/rebalance can then leak flusher processes that keep flushing and producing.

findings.title: Flusher restart leaks thread-mode workers
findings.body: When produce_to_pipe is set the worker is a threading.Thread. On unhealthy detection _ensure_processes_alive skips kill for threads because of the multiprocessing.Process check and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards, which starts a second thread sharing the same stopped/drift/backpressure/healthy Values while the old thread is still in its while not stopped.value loop. Both threads then flush the same shards and call produce, duplicating output and never reclaiming the old thread.

findings.title: Unused _create_process_for_shard would orphan running worker
findings.body: The helper _create_process_for_shard loops the shard map and calls _create_process_for_shards without stopping, joining, killing, or terminating the existing entry in self.processes, and it overwrites self.processes and self.buffers. It is currently dead code, but if wired up it would leak the old process/thread while two workers flush the same shards.
